This miscellaneous first appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'the MV Act') by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation granted by the Tribunal for the death of one Sangamesh @ Sangappa in a motor vehicle accident dated 15.02.2014.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. It is the case of the petitioners that they are the wife and children of deceased Sangamesh.
On 15.02.2014 at about 8-00 p.m., at Managuli village, the deceased was walking on the left side of the road.

A motorcycle bearing registration No.KA.28/EE.0226 (hereinafter referred as "the offending vehicle"), driven by its rider in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
Initially he was taken to BLDE Hospital, Vijayapura and from there to Gangamayi Hospital, Sholapur.
However, he died on 16.02.2014.
The petitioners have spent around Rs.1,00,000/- for his treatment.
As the wife and children, the petitioners were dependant on the deceased.
In respect of the accident, the case was registered against the rider of the offending vehicle.
The deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- p.m. by selling corn.
As the owner and insurer, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
4. Before the Tribunal, though duly served, respondent No.1 remained ex parte.
5. Though respondent No.2 appeared through counsel, did not chose to file written statement.
6. On behalf of the petitioners, petitioner No.2 is examined as P.W.1 and one witness as P.W.2.

They have relied upon Exs.P.1 to 12.
7.
Respondent No.2 got marked Ex.R.1, insurance policy.

Respondent No.2 has not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
10. During course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the income of the deceased ought to have been taken at Rs.10,000/- p.m.
No compensation is granted towards loss of future prospects.
11. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays to dismiss the appeal.
12. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the records.
13. Through the testimony of P.W.1, petitioners have proved their relationship with the deceased.
After detailed investigation, the concerned police have filed chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the offending vehicle was covered by a valid policy.

Considering the oral and documentary evidence placed on record, the Tribunal has rightly held that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle Smt.Indumati And Ors vs Sri.Shivaling And Anr on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81129386/

sentences.text:
Therefore, the only question that is to be decided is whether the quantum of compensation granted by the Tribunal is just and reasonable under the following heads:
15. Loss of dependency:-

The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove that the deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- p.m. Therefore, the Tribunal has justified in considering the income of the deceased on notional basis.
Since the accident is of the year 2014, based on minimum wages, the income should have been considered at Rs.7,500/- instead of Rs.5,000/- p.m.
Based on the medical records, the age of the deceased is correctly taken as 40 years and appropriate multiplier 15.

Since the deceased was coming under the age group of 40 to 50 years, as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma's case), 25% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects, which is not considered by the Tribunal.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma's case)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
25%
of Rs.7,500/- comes to Rs.1,875/- and therefore, the income of the deceased is required to be taken at Rs.9,375/- p.m.
Since there are three dependants, 1/3rd deduction towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased is correct.
The remaining 2/3rd is required to be taken into consideration for calculation loss of dependency.
With these components, the loss of dependency comes to Rs.9,375 x 12 x 15 x 2/3 = Rs.11,25,000/-.
Thus, the petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.11,25,000/- as against Rs.6,00,120/- granted by the Tribunal.
16. Loss of consortium:-
The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of consortium and Rs.25,000/- under the head loss of love and affection.

As per National Insurance Company Limited V. Pranay Sethi and (2018) 18 SCC 130 others2 (Pranay Sethi's case),
under the head loss of consortium, the wife, parents and children of the deceased are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each.

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for Rs.1,20,000/- as against Rs.30,000/-.
When compensation is granted under the head loss of consortium, no separate compensation is required to be granted under the head loss of love and affection.
Therefore, Rs.25,000/- granted under the head loss of love and affection is disallowed.
17. Medical expenses, attendant, conveyance expenses:-
It is pertinent to note that for two days, the deceased was under treatment, initially at BLDE hospital, Vijayapura and thereafter at Gangamayi Hospital, Sholapur.
The petitioners have produced medical bills for a sum of Rs.16,738/-.
Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal has rightly (2017) 16 SCC 680 granted compensation in sum of Rs.22,000/- and it does not calls for any interference.

18. Loss to estate and Funeral expenses:-
The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head loss to estate and Rs.25,000/- under the head funeral and transportation expenses.

When major compensation is granted under the head loss of dependency, as per Pranay Sethi's case referred to supra, under the conventional head of loss to estate and funeral expenses (which includes transportation charges), a sum of Rs.15,000/- each is required to be granted.

Therefore, compensation under the heads loss to estate and Smt.Indumati And Ors vs Sri.Shivaling And Anr on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81129386/
4 funeral expenses is reduced to Rs.15,000/- each.
